Alex —

Thanks for the clear overview. Attached is a starter worksheet that walks through three scenarios (conservative/typical/accelerated) and two pricing approaches: (A) levelized unit price with annual prepay credits and (B) explicit step discounts by year. Highlights:

- We typically offer an incremental discount ladder for multi-year prepays (example: 10% year1, 18% year2, 24% year3 on list for 3-year deals) when customers commit to annual prepay.
- For phased ramps we model the committed capacity as a schedule of monthly TPM equivalents; unused prepay can be carried forward within the same contract year but not retroactively applied to prior invoices.
- We support a formal "ramp-in" schedule where reserved units are provisioned in phases — billing is aligned to the committed units for each year; burst capacity is available at an add-on rate.

Questions for you to help refine the numbers:
- Do you need hard carryover across years (i.e., unused y1 credits applied to y2)?
- Any required SLA exceptions or high-availability regions? (US-only is fine for pricing)
- Are you open to a 3-year annual prepay vs. a single multi-year prepaid invoice?

Team —

Read Marissa's draft. Negotiation guidance (short):

1) Discount ladder (annual prepay, 3-year):
   - Year 1 prepay: 10% off list
   - Year 2 prepay: 18% off list (applies to year2 committed units)
   - Year 3 prepay: 24% off list

2) Carryover: allow carryforward within the *following* contract year up to 20% of the next year's committed units (prevents overhang risk). Full cross-year carryover unlimited creates accounting and capacity exposure.

3) Upgrade credit: if they accelerate commitment (e.g., move from 50->75 TPM in Y2), credit unused y1 units at the Y2 price for up to 12 months. No retroactive refunds.

4) SLA and burst: keep SLA standard; offer burst capacity with a 1.3x premium and optional burst reserve pool for launch windows.

5) Approval thresholds: anything with >20% concession to list requires my sign-off.

Recommend we present the counter as a clean table + short legal bullets. I'll approve the numbers above; Marissa/Soosin, run this by pricing/legal for the exact language.

-Karthik
